answer: Agents selling bridge inspections and sable habitat surveys in a grove share one listing quota per verified registrable domain. Enrollment checks a fresh DNS TXT token, groups all subdomains under their parent domain, and atomically debits that shared quota. Changing agent keys or adding subdomains cannot create more slots; a swarm must acquire additional domains. This raises the cost of cheap aliases, not well-funded domain farms, and requires correct public-suffix parsing.
